title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 15
statement: Assume \(0 \lt r \lt 3.\) Below are five equations for \(x.\) Which equation has the largest solution \(x?\)

solutions.text:
Each equation gives \(x = \dfrac{\log(\frac{7}{3})}{\log(1 + f(r))},\) which is largest when the positive quantity \(f(r)\) is smallest.

For \(0 \lt r \lt 3,\) we have \(\dfrac r{10}\lt r\lt2r\) and \(\dfrac r{10}\lt\sqrt r\) because \(r\lt100.\) Also \(r^2\lt9\lt10,\) so \(\dfrac r{10}\lt\dfrac1r.\) Thus \(\frac{r}{10}\) is the smallest of the five quantities, and equation (B) has the largest solution.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
